twitch.endpoint: irc://irc.chat.twitch.tv:6697 (TLS; wss://irc-ws.chat.twitch.tv:443 is the same protocol)
twitch.requires: nothing — an anonymous justinfan connection reads public chat
twitch.operator_action: name a channel: `--twitch-channel <login>` or chat.twitch_channels in config
twitch.note: Anonymous connections cannot send, moderate or whisper; xPST never asks for a chat token, so the connection is read-only by construction rather than by policy.

youtube.requires: OAuth token with youtube.readonly or youtube.force-ssl, and a broadcast that is live now (the activeLiveChatId only exists while a video is live)
youtube.operator_action: connect the channel with `xpst auth youtube`, then go live once
youtube.note: 5 quota units per poll against a 10,000-unit daily default, so 2,000 polls is the whole day. Never exercised live from this repository: the connected channel answers 403 'not enabled for live streaming', which is why a read refuses with live_not_enabled rather than an empty feed.

kick.requires: nothing — an anonymous guest token and a public channel subscription
kick.operator_action: name a channel: `--kick-channel <slug>` or chat.kick_channels in config
kick.note: UNDOCUMENTED PATH. Kick publishes no chat read endpoint: /public/v1/chat is send and delete only, and the documented alternative is the chat.message.sent webhook event, which needs a registered app and a public callback. Community libraries still point at a public Pusher app key that Kick has retired (Pusher answers 4001 on every cluster); kick.com's own page now mints an anonymous guest token at web.kick.com/api/v1/realtime/auth/connection and connects to its own Centrifugo service. Connection, subscription and heartbeat are proven from this repository; no chat publication has been observed yet, so the row stays unverified.
